findings.title: Networking share larkspur-core-network is lost: ec2:Subnet, ec2:TransitGateway, route53resolver:ResolverRule
findings.detail: Shared by account 111111111112 with organization o-larkspur0001. It is scoped to the source organization or one of its OUs and stops applying when the account leaves. What the documentation says happens: ec2:Subnet: existing participant resources continue to run in the subnet; no new resources can be created in it, while existing ones can still be modified, described and deleted (subnets can only be shared inside one organization). Potentially affected: ec2:RunInstances, rds:CreateDBInstance in use may target the shared resources; confirm. ec2:Subnet can only be shared inside one organization, so it cannot be re-shared with the account once it has left. ec2:TransitGateway: existing transit gateway attachments remain functional; the account can no longer describe the transit gateway or create new attachments, and either side can delete the attachments. The account uses ec2:CreateTransitGatewayVpcAttachment, which needs the share: that stops working. route53resolver:ResolverRule: traffic is affected at once, the rule's associations with the account's VPCs are removed and Resolver answers those queries from the remaining rules at once (an OU-scoped rule keeps its associations only when it is also shared with the destination OU). Ask the owner to re-share the resources with the account directly before the move, with external principals allowed, and accept the invitation after the move.

findings.title: 4 AWSReservedSSO_* role(s) are deleted from the account: AWSReservedSSO_AdministratorAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_PaymentsEngineer_*, AWSReservedSSO_ReadOnlyAccess_*, AWSReservedSSO_DataPlatformOperator_*
findings.detail: When the account leaves the organization, Identity Center cleans up the resources it created in the account; the documentation names the service-linked role, and the IAM roles provisioned for permission sets (path /aws-reserved/sso.amazonaws.com/us-east-1/) go with the instance's control over the account, so plan for them to disappear and confirm in IAM after the move. Anything that names these roles breaks: resource and trust policies, KMS key policies, S3 bucket policies, EKS access entries, pipelines and tools that assume them, and CloudTrail history keeps the old ARNs. The target instance provisions new roles with a different random suffix, so references have to be updated, not restored. The exact suffix is only visible in IAM; offline the roles are known by their pattern. 1 of them (AWSReservedSSO_DataPlatformOperator_*) are provisioned without any assignment and are already unused; deprovisioning the permission set from the account before the move removes them cleanly.

findings.title: Permission set PaymentsEngineer: 2 assignment(s) removed when the account leaves (group Payments-Engineers, user oncall.payments)
findings.detail: Account assignments exist only for accounts inside the organization that owns the instance. When the account leaves o-larkspur0001, Identity Center cleans up its metadata and resources for the account and a standalone account no longer works with Identity Center, so these 2 assignment(s) stop granting access at once. The target instance has no permission set named PaymentsEngineer. Create one there (or choose an equivalent) before re-assigning the 2 principal(s), who have to exist in identity store d-fern0000001 under the target instance.

findings.detail: Account assignments exist only for accounts inside the organization that owns the instance. When the account leaves o-larkspur0001, Identity Center cleans up its metadata and resources for the account and a standalone account no longer works with Identity Center, so these 1 assignment(s) stop granting access at once. The target instance has a permission set with the same name; re-assign the principals to it once the account has joined. They are matched by name only: identity store d-fern0000001 is a different directory, so the users and groups are different objects there. findings.title: Access is re-created in the target Identity Center instance, not moved
findings.detail: Assignments are not copied between instances. The target instance uses identity store d-fern0000001 (the source uses d-lark0000001); users and groups there are separate objects even when their names match, so each assignment is re-created by name after the account has accepted the invitation. Permission set names that exist in both instances: AdministratorAccess, ReadOnlyAccess. Missing in the target: PaymentsEngineer.
